Consequence estimation. bgev_mle() restricts estimation delta > 0. matches revised reference, whose estimation routine uses delta >= 0, loses nothing interest: bimodality occurs delta > 0 (delta = 0 ordinary GEV). distribution functions (dbgev(), pbgev(), …) still accept full delta > -1; estimator restricted. title: Maximum Likelihood Estimation for the BGEV Distribution
text: convergence — optim code (0 = success). agree — whether several independent starts reached maximum (practical “global?” signal). admissible — whether returned optimum regular interior maximum: positive-definite Hessian eigenvalue ratio 1e-6. multistart keeps best admissible optimum rejects spurious / singular ones; admissible = FALSE warns inference trustworthy . boundary — proximity data parameter-dependent support endpoint, usual regularity conditions fail. optimum — gradient norm, Hessian positive-definiteness eigenvalue ratio estimate. bgev_profile_likelihood() complements profile curve parameter — check Otiniano et al. use confirm optimum global.
code: x   <- rbgev(300, mu = 0, sigma = 1, xi = 0.2, delta = 1) fit <- bgev_mle(x) round(fit$par, 3) #>     mu  sigma     xi  delta  #> -0.004  0.918  0.315  1.232 c(loglik = fit$loglik, convergence = fit$convergence,   admissible = fit$admissible, agree = fit$agree) #>      loglik convergence  admissible       agree  #>   -340.5378      0.0000      1.0000      0.0000

title: Maximum Likelihood Estimation for the BGEV Distribution
text: study 13,500 fits (45 cells, 300 replications) simulated known parameters refit, mu = 0, sigma = 1, xi {−0.4, −0.2, 0, 0.2, 0.4}, delta {0.25, 1, 3} n {100, 250, 500}. script benchmarks/mc_study.R. Convergence 93–100% every cell (maximum failure rate 6%). results summarize two decision-relevant findings; static, taken run. estimator consistent well-calibrated regular regime (xi >= -0.2): bias → 0, RMSE falls like 1/sqrt(n), Wald coverage observed-information Hessian near nominal 0.95. Wald 95% coverage xi (delta = 1). Target 0.95. boundary (xi = -0.4) model non-regular: parameter-dependent support makes MLE non-normal, Wald coverage collapses worsens n (0.84 → 0.39 → 0.08) RMSE shrink. package flags admissibility gate, rejects fits: Admissible rate (positive-definite-Hessian gate), n = 500. Wald coverage holds gate accepts ~100% fits; fails rejects 88–90%. user checks fit$admissible steered away exactly fits whose Hessian-based standard errors trusted. boundary cells, parametric-bootstrap profile-likelihood intervals appropriate alternative Wald intervals.

title: Maximum Likelihood Estimation for the BGEV distribution — bgev_mle
text: fit carries diagnostics (convergence, agreement across starts, support-boundary check) BGEV support depends parameters, usual regularity conditions can fail near boundary. regime Hessian/Wald standard errors reliable; use parametric bootstrap instead (planned future version). Although BGEV distribution defined delta > -1, estimation restricted delta > 0. deliberate: bimodality – purpose model – occurs delta > 0, delta < 0 density unbounded x = mu (transform derivative (delta + 1)|x - mu|^delta diverges), giving singular likelihood whose global maximum spurious spike data point. revised BGEV reference estimates delta >= 0 reason. search run reparametrised scale – log(sigma) log(delta) – sigma > 0 delta > 0 hold automatically. remaining penalty guards data-dependent support (observations beyond fitted endpoint), box constraint transformed away. Among multistart results, fit returned highest-likelihood one whose Hessian optimum positive-definite (genuine interior maximum, rejecting spurious spikes); admissible FALSE none qualified. Estimates reported natural scale.
